content.title: About
content.content: Soft shell crab is a crab that has recently molted, shedding its hard exoskeleton and leaving only a thin, edible shell. It has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp texture that resembles other seafood.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft shell crabs are harvested during the molting period when their shells are still soft.
In Japan, soft shell crab is a prized delicacy often served in sushi and tempura.
Crabs can molt several times a year, but only during molting are they suitable as soft shell.
The whole crab—including head, tail, and legs—is usually served.
When cooked properly, the meat stays moist and does not become dry.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Soft shell crab provides high‑quality marine protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafoods, it contains very little fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of omega‑3
items.content: It contains beneficial omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The crab supplies B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for normal metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Crab is rich in zinc, selenium, and copper, minerals that aid immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to crab, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Although low in fat, crab contains cholesterol, so people with hypercholesterolemia should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Potential toxins
items.content: Crabs harvested from polluted waters can accumulate heavy metals and toxins; purchase only from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soft shell crab is commonly deep‑fried, baked in a batter, or grilled. It can be served whole, split in half, or used in salads, sushi, and pasta dishes. Before cooking, rinse the crab under cold water and pat dry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store soft shell crab in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a vacuum‑sealed bag for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen crab in the refrigerator before use.
